title: "Reference"
subtitle: "Every option the cascade extension accepts."
description: "The complete cascade behaviour: the two options, the per-heading attribute and class, how divs are handled, and what happens outside RevealJS."
---

## Enabling the filter

```yaml
filters:
  - cascade
```

## Options

```yaml
extensions:
  cascade:
    depth: 1
    keep-hrule: false
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `depth` | integer | unset | How many levels of the chain to repeat, counted from the slide level. Unset repeats the whole chain. |
| `keep-hrule` | boolean | `false` | Whether `---` survives in formats other than RevealJS. |

: Document and project options. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[16,12,12,60]"}

## Per-heading control

| Written on a heading | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `{cascade-depth="1"}` | Overrides `depth` for the chain starting at that heading. |
| `{.no-cascade}` | The heading stays on its own slide and is never carried forward. |

: The attribute and the class. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[30,70]"}

An override applies to the chain that begins at the annotated heading.
The document-level setting resumes at the next heading at or above slide level.

## Divs

A `---` inside a div splits the slide there too: the div is closed, the chain repeated, and an identical div reopened around what follows.

```markdown
## Results

::: {.column-margin}

A side note, first part.

---

Second part, still in the margin, on a new slide.

:::
```

Two exceptions are left alone, because reopening them would break them:

- `.panel-tabset`;
- a cross-reference target, meaning a div whose identifier looks like `#tbl-…`, `#fig-…`, `#thm-…`, and so on.

## What is not a slide break

| Where the `---` is | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| In a fenced code block | Pandoc treats it as content, so the filter never sees it. |
| In a pipe table | It is a column separator, and is left alone. |

: Horizontal rules that are not breaks. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[36,64]"}

## Warnings

A cloned chain that skips a heading level, a `##` followed by a `####` with no `###` between, is reported at render time.
The output is still produced; the warning surfaces a structure that is usually accidental.

## Outside RevealJS

`---` is removed by default, since nothing there splits into slides.

```yaml
extensions:
  cascade:
    keep-hrule: true
```

keeps the horizontal rules as rules.

## Limitations

- RevealJS only. Elsewhere the filter either removes the rules or leaves them, and repeats nothing.
- `.panel-tabset` and cross-reference divs are not split.
